name: Submersible UV Steriliser
summary: A UVC lamp in a quartz sleeve that sits inside the tank or sump rather than inline on a hose. Six sizes from 4 to 20 W.
bestFor: Knocking out a green water bloom or running in a sump on a larger system.
highlights: 4 to 20 W UVC
Quartz glass sleeve
Goes directly in the tank or sump
watchOut: An open UV lamp in the display tank needs care, and it will not fix the nutrient imbalance behind an algae bloom.

name: Doctor 5
summary: Chihiros' latest electrolytic water-care unit. A reactor in the tank produces short-lived oxidisers to hold back algae and harmful bacteria, while the controller also watches temperature and shows it on a small screen and in the app.
bestFor: Freshwater planted tanks where you want algae prevention and a temperature alarm in one small gadget.
highlights: Micro-electrolysis reactor with magnetic connections
Three modes; you enter your tank size during setup
Temperature monitoring with app and on-screen alerts
Bluetooth control via MyChihiros
Maker states it is safe for fish, shrimp and filter bacteria
watchOut: Only for water under 500 ppm TDS, and the reactor is a consumable that needs replacing.

name: Doctor Mate
summary: The small Doctor, sized for nano and small tanks up to about 125 L. It runs the same three plant, fish and shrimp modes as the larger unit, with Bluetooth control.
bestFor: Nano and small planted tanks, including shrimp tanks, that want an algae and bacteria hedge.
highlights: For tanks under 125 L
Three modes: plants, fish, shrimp
Bluetooth app control
Compact controller and square reactor
watchOut: Replacement reactors are an ongoing cost.

name: New Doctor
summary: The standard-size Chihiros Doctor, an electrolytic unit with separate plant, fish and shrimp modes. The plant mode targets algae, and the fish and shrimp modes aim at harmful bacteria. It comes with either Bluetooth app control or touch buttons.
bestFor: Mid-size and larger planted tanks where you want an extra tool against algae alongside good maintenance.
highlights: Three modes: plants, fish, shrimp
Bluetooth or touch-control versions
Reactor sits on the glass, controller outside
Suited to tanks from about 75 L up

specs.Tank size: About 20 to 30 US gal (75 to 115 L) and up

watchOut: It won't fix a light or nutrient imbalance, and the reactor needs periodic replacement.

name: reeflexUV
summary: reeflexUV is an inline UV clarifier that goes on your canister's return hose. A reflector inside bounces the UV back through the water, so it gets more done per watt than a plain unit, and it kills free-floating algae that turns water green.
bestFor: Planted tanks prone to green water, or anyone wanting a bit of extra clarity and pathogen control.
highlights: Fits inline on the filter return
Internal reflector boosts effective UV dose
Clears green water from suspended algae
Three sizes to match tank volume and filter flow
watchOut: It does nothing for algae growing on plants or glass, and the lamp needs replacing about once a year.

name: reeflexUV+e
summary: The reeflexUV+e is the WiFi version of the reeflexUV. You can run it constantly, on a daily schedule or linked to other Eheim devices, and it tells you by e-mail when the lamp is due for a change.
bestFor: Larger planted tanks where you want UV only for set hours, or want it tied into an Eheim digital setup.
highlights: Constant, daily cycle or coupled modes over WiFi
Booster mode for a short, intense treatment
Lamp change reminder by e-mail
Switches off automatically when you open it to change the lamp
watchOut: It costs about twice as much as the standard reeflexUV for the same job, so only worth it if you will use the scheduling.

name: ClearTronic
summary: An inline UV-C clarifier that plumbs into your filter outlet hose and clears green water and free-floating bacteria. The ballast is built into the body, so there is no separate box to find room for in the cabinet. The lamp and quartz sleeve come out with a quick-release for cleaning.
bestFor: Canister-filtered tanks prone to green water, or keepers who want an extra safeguard against outbreaks.
highlights: 7, 9 or 11 W UV-C for tanks up to 250, 400 or 600 litres
Integrated ballast, compact 33 cm body
Quick-release for lamp changes and quartz cleaning
Connection accessories included
watchOut: UV lamps lose strength over time and need replacing roughly yearly, and UV does not fix the nutrient or light imbalance behind algae.

name: AUV UV-C Lamp
summary: A submersible UV-C lamp that sits in the tank or sump, from 3 to 14 W, rated for 500 to 2,600 litres. Most sizes come with a shade to block visible glare.
bestFor: Tanks or sumps with green water or where you want to cut free-floating bacteria.
highlights: 3 to 14 W
Rated for up to 500 to 2,600 litres
Submersible
Light shield on 6 W and up
watchOut: UV-C can harm eyes and degrade some plastics; never look at the lit lamp and keep it shielded.

name: ZUV Timer UV-C Lamp
summary: A submersible UV-C lamp with a built-in timer, from SunSun's Zhizhen line, rated for 1,800 to 2,600 litres. Three sizes, 10 to 14 W.
bestFor: Large tanks and sumps with green water.
highlights: Built-in timer
Rated for up to 1,800 to 2,600 litres
Light shield included
watchOut: Keep the lamp shielded and switched off when your hands are in the tank.

name: Nano Sterilizer / Algae Inhibitor
summary: Twinstar's electrolytic steriliser: a small controller outside the tank powers a reactor disc on the glass that produces short-lived oxidising radicals. The idea is to knock back algae spores and bacteria before they take hold, without a UV lamp or plumbing into the filter.
bestFor: Planted tanks up to about 250 L where you want an extra hedge against green water and algae, especially during the first months.
highlights: Four sizes: M3, M5, Nano and Nano Plus
Reactor mounts inside the tank, no filter plumbing
Maker states it is safe for fish, shrimp, plants and filter bacteria
Best started on a new tank before algae appears

specs.Install: Reactor disc on glass, controller outside the tank

watchOut: It supports, not replaces, balanced light, CO2 and nutrients, and the reactor disc needs replacing and descaling over time.
